nodes.label: email_log insert-before-send idempotency pattern
nodes.rationale: Insert email_log row BEFORE sending via Resend. Reversed order risks duplicates if the process crashes between send and log; the 'miss one' failure mode is recoverable (manual re-send) while 'send twice' undermines trust — asymmetric cost drives the ordering choice.

nodes.label: requireStaff() load-bearing helper (design)
nodes.rationale: Returns {id, role, email} for the logged-in staff user or throws 401; every staff Server Action begins with this call. Written once with full tests in phase 1, not touched again until MS-SSO migration.

nodes.label: Server-derived timezone rationale
nodes.rationale: Timezone is derived server-side from venue lat/lng via offline tz-lookup so it becomes derived state, not trusted user input; browser never sees or computes TZ, keeping the value tamper-proof and consistent.

nodes.label: Accordion-over-wizard navigation rationale
nodes.rationale: User wanted freedom to fill sections in any order; a wizard's strict gating would force a back-button cascade that complicates state. Accordion with per-section Done buttons (no auto-collapse on blur) gives the right level of structure without surprise behaviour.

nodes.label: Mapbox HK proximity-bias rationale
nodes.rationale: proximity (Victoria Harbour lng/lat) is the single highest-leverage knob to surface HK landmarks like HKCEC without restricting matches; no country filter preserves global fallback for non-HK addresses.

nodes.label: Nominatim-over-Mapbox decision rationale
nodes.rationale: Direct curl tests against five providers proved Mapbox has near-zero coverage of HK/Asian landmarks (HKCEC search returned a Vietnam result 1,679km away); Nominatim returned the correct HKCEC lat/lon on first query. Zero setup friction (no key/billing) fits current staff-only scale (~500 searches/month) against Nominatim's 1 req/sec public-instance budget.

nodes.label: C1 — publishEvent ignored RLS denials (silent failure)
nodes.rationale: .update().eq() returns 0 affected rows when an organizer tries to publish another organizer's event, but the action returned success and revalidated — pure silent failure. Fixed by chaining .select('id').maybeSingle() and throwing when data is null.
nodes.norm_label: c1 — publishevent ignored rls denials (silent failure)

nodes.label: C4 — proxy signOut() cookie/response-object mismatch
nodes.rationale: signOut() wrote clear-cookies to res, but the function returned a different NextResponse.redirect() object, so the browser stayed signed in and the next visit triggered an infinite redirect loop. Fixed via a redirectWithCookies() helper that copies res.cookies onto the redirect — same bug class as the /auth/callback fix.

nodes.label: Inline base64 QR storage decision
nodes.rationale: QR PNGs are returned as inline base64 data URLs rather than stored in a Supabase Storage bucket — avoids adding a storage surface for a small (~3-5KB), on-demand-regenerable artifact.

nodes.label: Extract buildEventQrPng to lib/qr.ts decision
nodes.rationale: getEventQrPng() calls requireStaff(), but both the poster page and public registration page need QR generation without staff auth. Rather than dropping auth from the existing action (risky) the pure QR-byte generation is extracted to a shared lib/qr.ts helper; auth + RLS gating stays in each calling layer.

nodes.label: Registration-closed CSV export gate
nodes.rationale: CSV export button is gated on 'registration closed' = event.end_time < now() OR at max_attendees capacity, computed server-side at render time with no new schema field — avoids a stored state field for a derivable condition.

nodes.label: Idempotent UPDATE ... WHERE status != 'attended' race-safety pattern
nodes.rationale: markAttended and selfCheckIn both UPDATE ... WHERE registration_code = code AND status != 'attended', returning 0 rows on a race between staff-tablet and self-checkin or duplicate scans. Surfacing the 0-row case as a distinct 'already attended' error rather than reporting fake success follows the fail-visibly rule (CLAUDE.md rule 12).
nodes.norm_label: idempotent update ... where status != 'attended' race-safety pattern

nodes.label: Cross-event scan tolerance decision
nodes.rationale: markAttended does not require the staff member to own the event whose code was scanned, so a manager running check-in for multiple concurrent events from one tablet doesn't get spurious failures; the success toast shows the event title, making cross-event scans visible rather than silently blocked.

nodes.label: Idempotent check-in pattern (WHERE status != 'attended')
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md rule 12 (fail visibly) requires a second writer for the same code to get 'already attended' rather than silently re-stamping the timestamp; enforced via a conditional UPDATE guard.

nodes.label: Mockup-supersedes-vault-data-model conflict resolution (Rule 7)
nodes.rationale: Vault Data Model.md specced 3 numeric 1-5 ratings + free text; the user-provided mockup specified 5 categorical questions instead. Resolution: mockup is authoritative (explicit, newer instruction) per CLAUDE.md Rule 7 — conflicts are surfaced and a side is picked, not averaged.

nodes.label: Audit-insert-last, same-transaction rule
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md pivot-era hard rule: any transaction writing audit_events emits the audit event as the LAST statement before commit, since the chain trigger holds pg_advisory_xact_lock until commit — guarantees lock order == chain_seq order == chain order.

nodes.label: BASELINE-DELTAS §3.2 — chain_seq drawn inside advisory lock
nodes.rationale: Identity defaults evaluate at tuple formation before BEFORE triggers fire, so a pre-assigned chain_seq's order need not match lock-acquisition order; overwriting chain_seq inside the advisory lock guarantees correct ordering.
nodes.norm_label: baseline-deltas §3.2 — chain_seq drawn inside advisory lock

nodes.norm_label: cpd sprint 2 — design: security wrapper + audit path + attendee identity

nodes.label: D1 — Restrict write_audit_event grant (revoke authenticated EXECUTE)
nodes.rationale: Closes the audit-authenticity gap from Sprint 1: a malicious authenticated user could forge a legitimately-chained row with false actor claims by calling write_audit_event directly via PostgREST. Every audited mutation instead becomes a SECURITY DEFINER fn ending in the audit write; the postgres-owned definer inherits audit_writer's EXECUTE, so legitimate paths are unaffected.
nodes.norm_label: d1 — restrict write_audit_event grant (revoke authenticated execute)

nodes.label: ADR Finding 1 — PostgREST RPCs run as separate transactions
nodes.rationale: An app-level wrapper calling write_audit_event after a mutation runs the audit write in a separate transaction, violating audit-insert-last-same-transaction; forces the SECURITY DEFINER gate→mutation→audit-write-LAST shape.
nodes.norm_label: adr finding 1 — postgrest rpcs run as separate transactions

nodes.label: P2 — Global audit-chain lock discipline
nodes.rationale: The audit chain serializes all writes through one global advisory lock held for transaction duration; audited definer functions must complete slow work before the audit-write and have no side effects between audit-write and commit.

nodes.label: P3 — Behaviour-preserving TDD on rewritten surfaces
nodes.rationale: Check-in and event-publish are shipped surfaces converted to definer functions; capture current behaviour before rewrite, rewrite, re-run same tests, name any intentional delta (per-IP to per-event rate-limit change).

nodes.rationale: Per-IP→per-event rate-limit switch let invalid codes return before any rate-limit ran, removing brute-force protection; fixed by IP-limiting the guess path specifically without reintroducing the venue-NAT problem.

nodes.label: Q23 — UUID identity key + licence model
nodes.norm_label: q23 — uuid identity key + licence model

nodes.label: Q24 — per-body retention citation grounding
nodes.rationale: Six of eight launch bodies got primary-source retention citations (2–6yr range, no single default); HKIE and HKCR are verified absences, not search misses. The commonly-cited 7 years matches no body's actual clause.

nodes.label: Deterministic evaluator (bounded-grammar interpreter)
nodes.rationale: The CPD compliance verdict is a read-time projection of ledger rows against versioned config; built as a bounded-grammar interpreter, NOT a general rules engine (the deferred over-build). HKCR 16-type passive/active cap is the stress test.

nodes.label: Q30 — pass-through payments posture
nodes.rationale: Pass-through only, Stripe as placeholder direction, structured to stay outside HKMA SVF/MSO licensing; invoice-first through Milestone E (zero payment code).

nodes.label: CPD Passport (competitor)
nodes.rationale: Differentiator: Eventar offers real-time first-party attendance capture vs CPD Passport's self-report + ~30-working-day third-party verification.

nodes.label: Registration-timing fix (180-min seed offset)
nodes.rationale: Check-in window opens unconditionally at start−CHECKIN_OPEN_MINUTES (60min), closing registration; 45- and 90-min seed offsets both too short, widened to 180min for a ~120min registration window that outlasts prep + the 15-min demo.

nodes.label: External accrediting-body review (Sprint 3b gate)
nodes.rationale: One accrediting body + one organiser + one practitioner must review the ledger/lifecycle design before Sprint 3b's governance+engine is detailed into SQL; also resolves Q26. The long pole — only Ivan can schedule it.

nodes.label: credit_ledger hash chain has zero automated test coverage
nodes.norm_label: credit_ledger hash chain has zero automated test coverage

nodes.label: Hard Rule: Integrity is structural; domain is configuration
nodes.rationale: Any tamper-evidence/audit/actor-authenticity/append-only/tenancy/residency guarantee must be structural and unreachable by any config flag; domain-specific behaviour must be configuration data so new bodies onboard without a code change.
nodes.norm_label: hard rule: integrity is structural; domain is configuration

nodes.label: Hard Rule: Configuration is data; scaling is row-based
nodes.rationale: New bodies/organisers/cycles/roles are added as data rows, never new tables/columns/branches; if onboarding a body needs a migration or deploy, something configurable was hardwired. Hierarchy uses parent_body_id.
nodes.norm_label: hard rule: configuration is data; scaling is row-based

nodes.label: RFC 8785 JSON canonicalization (never hash raw JSONB)
nodes.norm_label: rfc 8785 json canonicalization (never hash raw jsonb)

nodes.label: Validation boundary (structural in DB, compliance in app)
nodes.norm_label: validation boundary (structural in db, compliance in app)

nodes.label: Single global hash chains kept
nodes.rationale: audit_events and credit_ledger each keep one global chain_seq-ordered chain; per-stream chains deferred until a measured write-concurrency profile shows the advisory lock is the bottleneck, not built against a hypothetical.

nodes.label: D.1 config-hash fork (pinned-in-hash vs chained-version-table)
nodes.rationale: Whether canonical config serialization sits on the ledger's hot write path (pinned-in-hash) or in a cheap chained config side-chain. Lean: chained-version-table. Highest-value open decision; logged as vault Q26.

nodes.label: Evaluator-versioning gap
nodes.rationale: Reproducing a past verdict needs rows + config-in-force + the evaluator (code) in force; the evaluator is pinned in neither D.1 arm. Current doctrine delivers input reproducibility, not verdict reproducibility.

nodes.label: HKCP — Hong Kong College of Physicians
nodes.norm_label: hkcp — hong kong college of physicians

nodes.label: CPD Sprint 3b Governance Outline
nodes.rationale: Deliberately a design outline not an implementation plan, so the external review can inform the two open shapes rather than pre-deciding them.

nodes.label: Body Reviewer Accreditation Workflow (Task 1)
nodes.rationale: Provisional default is a single manual reviewer queue per body, no SLA, no auto-approval, no member-DB integration; multi-reviewer/SLA/auto-approval each add real schema.

nodes.label: Post-Publish Accreditation Confirmation Granularity (Task 2)
nodes.rationale: Default is event-level confirmation (one flip, not per-attendee) with no new stored state; per-attendee would need its own table keyed on individual ledger/registration rows plus an unfreeze.

nodes.label: Body-Specific PDF Audit Response Format (Task 3)
nodes.rationale: Default is a standardised Eventar PDF (body logo inserted) rendered from the ledger projection; per-body form-mimicking is a real per-body content task, likely staying deferred to Sprint 5+.

nodes.label: Cross-Body Recognition Operational Mechanics (Task 4)
nodes.rationale: Q25 already locked recognition at the ledger level via event dual-accreditation; default is practitioner-declared only, no automation, which is the system's state without any 3b work.

nodes.label: Event Lifecycle decision-state machine
nodes.rationale: Five stored states (draft, pending_body_review, published, credited, cancelled) locked in Q23 item 4; attestation_status is a field on published events, not a separate state.

nodes.label: CPD Sprint 3b Engine Outline
nodes.rationale: Covers the engine that turns attendance into compliant credits, the MVP critical path, double-gated on Q26 plus the external body review; exists so the engine is designable fast once gates lift.

nodes.label: Three-Layer Open-Framework Line
nodes.rationale: Config/data layer fully open now; governance layer open interfaces with defaults; evaluator layer a bounded-grammar interpreter, NOT a general rules engine, extended on documented demand only.

nodes.label: body_rules versioned config DDL (E1)
nodes.rationale: Append-only effective-dated rule versions (effective_from + version_seq, active derived by query); rule content ungated (verified vs 8 bodies), versioning mechanism Q26-shaped.

nodes.label: Deterministic Evaluator evaluate_compliance() (E2)
nodes.rationale: Pure deterministic function projecting a licence's ledger against the body_rules version in force at each entry's valid_domain_time; no AI, no mutation; the single largest unbuilt engine unknown.

nodes.label: Bounded-Grammar Interpreter discipline
nodes.rationale: Evaluator interprets a fixed grammar (floors/caps/cores/units/cycle windows), not arbitrary logic; a body needing logic outside the grammar gets the grammar extended to their documented rule, not a configurable engine.

nodes.label: HKCR 16-subtype passive/active cap stress test
nodes.rationale: Storing 16 activity types is trivial; the evaluator must compute a passive/active cap aggregated across them under the rule version in force at each date; if it handles HKCR it handles the eight verified bodies.

nodes.label: Q26 Config-Hash Fork
nodes.rationale: Pinned-in-hash vs chained-version-table; decided from one behavioural fact (how a body handles mid-cycle rule changes); the single gate that unblocks E1-versioning, E5 and E2 in sequence.

nodes.label: Q27 Evaluator-Versioning
nodes.rationale: For a reproducible historical verdict the evaluator's own version (release tag/code hash) must be pinnable alongside the config version; decide when the first verdict is exported.

nodes.label: RFC 8785 canonical serialization
nodes.rationale: Applied before any config hash regardless of which Q26 arm wins; both arms hash canonicalized config, only where differs.

nodes.label: Bitemporal rule-version evaluation (valid_domain_time)
nodes.rationale: A December activity is judged under December's rules even if evaluated in March.

nodes.label: Issuance: attendance x rules to ledger entries (E3)
nodes.rationale: On published-to-credited transition a deterministic job reads attendance x the body_rules version in force and writes credit_earned via record_credit_entry; store all credits incl. unmatched-body cases, filter in a view, never drop silently.
nodes.norm_label: issuance: attendance x rules to ledger entries (e3)

nodes.label: Roster ingestion + verification badges (E4)
nodes.rationale: Self-declared-until-roster is the correct default; verification is an additive trust signal not a tamper surface; an unverified licence is flagged, never blocked. Gated on Q7 (does the pilot body provide a roster).

nodes.label: Retroactive-Trust-Upgrade Model (E5)
nodes.rationale: One problem, three instances (event confirmation, licence verification, future signals); three candidate mechanisms (leave-pinned, append credit_adjusted, project trust at query time), each with a real cost; coupled to Q26 because the clean answer differs by arm.

nodes.label: External-Voice Review going-in position
nodes.rationale: The one external review (one accrediting body, one organiser, one practitioner) that gates all of Sprint 3b; a good meeting makes the engine designable not designed.

nodes.label: Three Categories of Review Items
nodes.rationale: Body-dependent facts (ask), safe defaults (confirm), and open internal design the review informs but does not close (evaluator + retro-trust model); if category 3 is omitted from notes, review-done gets misread as 3b-unblocked.

nodes.label: The Seven Review Questions (Q1-Q7)
nodes.rationale: Four confirmations (Q1 reviewers, Q2 confirmation, Q4 cross-body, Q6 storage grammar), three real body decisions (Q3 PDF, Q5 fork input, Q7 roster), one architecturally load-bearing (Q5).

nodes.label: Q5 behavioural framing rule
nodes.rationale: The body cannot pick pinned-in-hash vs chained-version-table; ask only about their rule-change behaviour and never mention hash architecture; we pick the arm from that one behavioural fact afterward.

nodes.label: POC + Engagement Plan
nodes.rationale: Build the POC/demo pack first, trial with NGOs + internal meetings, then engage the accrediting body; never walk in empty-handed. Slots under roadmap-to-mvp, does not replace the milestone spine.

nodes.label: Workstream D Production Deployment (D0-D7)
nodes.rationale: D0 deploy go/no-go DECIDED 2026-07-11: HOLD, demo pack first; D1 CI harness proceeds deploy-neutral; D2-D7 parked until Ivan flips.

nodes.label: Ledger demo driver (P2)
nodes.rationale: The differentiator moment: record_credit_entry then verify_ledger_chain valid, then a direct owner tamper rejected (42501) and a post-hoc edit caught by the chain - records that cannot be silently altered.

nodes.label: Singapore project provisioning (ap-southeast-1)
nodes.rationale: Fresh replay of the full migration chain validates the portability fixes; trials collect real PII so they land on Singapore not Seoul (PDPO posture); Seoul becomes dev/staging.

nodes.label: Resend cutover
nodes.rationale: Remove devEmailStub at 3 call sites (registerForEvent + both email actions) per the Phase-7 removal protocol; re-entry criterion fires with the first NGO trial.

nodes.label: Turnstile keys + wiring
nodes.rationale: Gates public exposure (ADR Finding 2); documented interim for invite-only trials is accepting the risk with existing per-IP rate limits, but provisioning keys is recommended.

nodes.label: Milestone A Demo-ready
nodes.rationale: Exit: prod URL live on Singapore, real emails, Turnstile or explicit interim, privacy notice; run sheet rehearsed under 15 min twice; ledger demo shows chain + tamper rejection; one-pagers + price approved.

nodes.label: Phase P2 Engagement (internal to NGO to body)
nodes.norm_label: phase p2 engagement (internal to ngo to body)

nodes.label: Milestone B Function proven in the field
nodes.rationale: 3+ real events end-to-end on prod, 50+ real check-ins, zero data-integrity incidents, friction list triaged, 1+ NGO referenceable.
nodes.norm_label: milestone b function proven in the field

nodes.label: Milestone C Body engaged
nodes.rationale: Meeting held (HKCP or MCHK), all 7 questions answered, Q26 resolvable, pilot proposal delivered with a price.

nodes.label: Milestone D Pilot agreed
nodes.rationale: Pilot terms accepted (scope, events, price, timeline); Sprint 3b executes with real answers and rejoins the roadmap spine at M2.

nodes.label: HKCP outreach + MCHK fallback (parallel-track rule)
nodes.rationale: Target the CPD/education committee secretariat; if HKCP is silent for 2 weeks send MCHK - never single-thread the long pole.

nodes.label: Pre-committed re-evaluation trigger (wedge review)
nodes.rationale: If after Milestone B + 4 weeks of active outreach no body will meet, that is data not a delay: wedge review (organiser-first or white-label), not more speculative backend. Written down while morale is high.

nodes.label: Execution Plans Index B-E
nodes.rationale: Companion to program-plan-A-to-E; gives B a runbook, C a checklist, and M2/M3/D/E honest skeletons each stating its detailing gate - the event that must happen before its full plan can be written without guessing.

nodes.label: B Deploy runbook + trial cadence
nodes.rationale: Detailing gate NONE - executable now on Ivan's D0 flip; each deploy step verified before the next, becomes docs/ops/deploy-runbook.md as it executes.

nodes.label: C Body engaged checklist
nodes.rationale: 7+2 questions rehearsed and answered; same-week close-out captures answers verbatim to Decisions Log; re-evaluation trigger stands (B done + 4 weeks dead outreach).

nodes.label: M2 CPD engine (Sprint 3b) skeleton
nodes.rationale: Detailing gate is C's answers + Q26 resolution; body_rules shape depends on the Q26 arm, evaluator grammar on real rule semantics, reviewer workflow + PDF format are literally two review questions - detailing SQL before C = building on guesses.

nodes.label: M3 Signed & verifiable skeleton
nodes.rationale: Detailing gate M2 shipped + unfreeze scope + body's PDF answer; covers AWS/KMS ops, sign-certificate, verify-record public URL, TOTP mandatory, pg_cron email jobs, unfreeze wave 1.

nodes.label: D/M4 Pilot-complete skeleton
nodes.rationale: Detailing gate M3 + pilot contract + pilot event dates; organiser accreditation UI, CPD Ledger wallet v1, walk-in mechanism, pilot ops playbook, evidence pack, invoice.

nodes.label: E Production-ready skeleton
nodes.rationale: Detailing gate pilot retro + per-wave triggers; acceptance test is body #2 onboards without hand-holding.

nodes.label: E production waves W1-W7
nodes.rationale: W1 external activities + evidence locker, W2 session/track model, W3 auditor portal, W4 org self-serve admin (role-scoped concurrency), W5 comms v2, W6 reports v2, W7 production hardening incl. Stripe pass-through outside HKMA SVF/MSO licensing.

nodes.label: Detailing gate discipline
nodes.rationale: Writing detailed SQL/UI plans ahead of the gate that resolves their unknowns is exactly the mistake the standing rules prohibit; each skeleton names the event that must happen first.

nodes.label: Market Realignment analysis
nodes.rationale: Maps what a production-grade CPD/event platform is expected to do (competitor teardown + 12 body documents + UI refs) vs what Eventar is building; sharpens the review and stocks the post-review backlog, must not become a reason to build ahead of validation.

nodes.label: Competitor CPD Passport
nodes.rationale: Manual entry + certificate upload + lock-flag with admin override + self-report with 30-working-day third-party verification; structural weaknesses Eventar beats with first-party attendance and a tamper-evident chain.

nodes.label: External activities + evidence locker
nodes.rationale: The gap between an event-attendance tool and a CPD platform (the backfill/new-joiner mechanism); manual entry with per-body taxonomies + Supabase Storage evidence (retention per body) + a verification-tier field so external entries coexist without diluting the chain.

nodes.label: Verification tiers (attendance_verified/organiser_attested/self_declared)
nodes.rationale: A per-entry trust field so scanned-at-venue credits keep the strongest tier and the evaluator applies tier-aware caps (e.g. self-study ceilings).

nodes.label: Session-level model (multi-track/per-session)
nodes.rationale: Matters specifically if the pilot event is a conference (multi-room, per-hour points); two phases - cheap schema readiness now, full multi-track UI post-M4. Ivan call: what shape is the intended pilot event.

nodes.label: Verify-this-record public URL
nodes.rationale: The hash-registry lookup page (paste/scan a record ref to chain-verified); nearly free given the registry, converts the integrity story into something a body clerk can touch. Explicit S4 deliverable.

nodes.label: Calendar links (.ics/Google/Outlook)
nodes.rationale: Designed pre-pivot (lib/calendarLinks.ts), never built; backend-only email template addition, freeze-safe; candidate for demo-pack polish week.

nodes.label: Walk-in handling at the door
nodes.rationale: Small design (staff-created registration inside TC), needed by any real event with door traffic; design note now, build at first trial feedback.

nodes.label: Online-CME MCQ assessment gate
nodes.rationale: HKAM's iCMECPD requires QR capture plus MCQ completion for e-learning points; defer with a hard trigger (first online/hybrid accredited event), state as a scope boundary in the body-review script.

nodes.label: CPD Ledger naming (Q29)
nodes.rationale: Resolved 2026-07-12: Eventar's module is the CPD Ledger; CPD Passport retired, reserved for the competitor (brand collision).

nodes.label: Paid ticketing excluded (Q21)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately excluded; invoice-first billing is zero-code for pilot. Re-entry trigger: first organiser asks to charge attendees - then a payments decision, not a feature toggle.

nodes.label: Compliance projection (floors/caps/cycles)
nodes.rationale: Not raw totals (the competitor's weakness) but 34.5 of 50, Category A floor met, on track - the 3b evaluator's exact job; body docs confirm its bounded-grammar shape (HKCR 30 CatB of 90; HKIE per-category floors).

nodes.label: Milestone A Executable Plan
nodes.rationale: Task-by-task TDD plan delivering everything Milestone A promises; demo scripts run against the LOCAL Supabase stack only (never Seoul, where credit_ledger is append-only), live migrations via CLI db push.

nodes.label: scripts/demo/lib.ts local-only helper
nodes.rationale: Refuses anything that isn't 127.0.0.1; T1 shipped with sqlLocal (direct pg connection) replacing psqlLocal (docker exec) because spawnSync docker times out from nested child processes in sandboxed harnesses.

nodes.label: seed-demo.ts fixture
nodes.rationale: Idempotent seed: operator, practitioner, Clinical Update Seminar 2026 as draft (start now+45min so registration+check-in windows overlap mid-demo), 6 attendees.

nodes.label: render-emails.ts
nodes.rationale: Renders confirmation + reminder; reminder's cid: image swapped for a data-URI QR because a browser can't show cid attachments.

nodes.label: ledger-demo.ts trust-moment driver
nodes.rationale: declare_licence to verify_licence to self_check_in to record_credit_entry; service-role UPDATE blocked (42501); superuser tamper caught by the ledger verifier - the demo's differentiator moment.

nodes.label: CI replay-and-verify harness
nodes.rationale: Throwaway local stack: supabase db reset (all migrations + seed) then assert both chain verifiers green, tamper the first probe row, expect detection; GitHub Actions job runs it on push/PR.

nodes.label: set_staff_role() audited definer function
nodes.rationale: Column-level revoke update(role) so fixture INSERTs keep working but role changes become definer-only; writes staff_role_changed audit event LAST; negative test asserts SQLSTATE 42501 specifically.

nodes.label: Residual grant hygiene batch
nodes.rationale: revoke all from public then re-grant intended roles for self_check_in/require_active_staff/pseudonymise_user, ending with a self-verifying DO block asserting the has_function_privilege matrix; plus fail-loud fixture cleanup (mustDelete).

nodes.label: Collateral drafts (CPD Ledger naming)
nodes.rationale: One-pager + trust one-pager + outreach email; the word Passport appears nowhere (Q29).

nodes.label: Phase-completion protocol (three lenses + backtest)
nodes.rationale: Dev-lens + separate user-lens + security-reviewer agent (Tasks 9-10), then backtest; grant matrix re-verified against LIVE proacl queries, never migration text.

nodes.label: Hard Rule 11 grant posture
nodes.rationale: Audited-mutation tables revoke direct writes at the grant level (service_role included, since it has BYPASSRLS); proven by a negative test asserting 42501.

nodes.label: Organiser IA + Data-Design Spec
nodes.rationale: Drill-down on the organiser web app navigation, per-module contents, and input/output flows; feeds task #8 design implementation and the M2 unfreeze scope.

nodes.label: Left sidebar app-shell + counted pill-tabs
nodes.rationale: witan/Cadre pattern - 8 nav areas outgrow the shipped 3-part top bar; two-level nav (sidebar global, tabs within-event); mobile bottom nav with Scan as the prominent center action.

nodes.label: Eight organiser nav areas
nodes.rationale: Dashboard, Events, Participants, Accreditation & Compliance, Check-in, Communications, Reports/Analytics, Settings/Admin - subtracts payment settings (Q21), custom fields, integrations.

nodes.label: Participants (person-level, PDPO purpose-limited)
nodes.rationale: NOT a marketing CRM; registration data was collected to run events not for cold outreach; person-level view derived from event participation, no cold-contact imports, no campaign lists.

nodes.label: Accreditation & Compliance (organiser view)
nodes.rationale: Renamed from CPD Passport per Q29; the wallet is attendee-side, the organiser-side module is event accreditations + body relationships + roster eligibility signals; organisers see outcomes, never edit licences.

nodes.label: Needs-attention queue
nodes.rationale: LoopAI priority-tasks motif; every row is actionable and deep-links to the fix, nothing informational-only; the notification bell must open this same queue, not a second feed.

nodes.label: Per-event readiness strip
nodes.rationale: Cadre motif; one glance answers is this event ready to run (registered fraction, speakers confirmed, accreditation, reminder scheduled, survey armed).

nodes.label: Data presentation rules (intuition layer)
nodes.rationale: Counts live in the chrome; meters/deltas/pills over raw numbers; one-color-one-meaning; tabular-nums right-aligned for regulatory point values; progressive disclosure row-drawer-page; compliance facts repeat wherever the person/event appears.

nodes.label: Eligibility flag (property of the row)
nodes.rationale: Licence lapsed - credits will not post, shown wherever the person appears (roster, check-in, participant list); a lapse discovered at the desk is a credit that silently never posts.

nodes.label: Program Plan A to E
nodes.rationale: Phase-level work plan (scope in/out, spec, exit criteria, rough execution) for the consolidated roadmap; the contract that each phase-start executable plan implements.

nodes.label: End-state commitment (production-ready checklist)
nodes.rationale: Functionally complete against the block map, operationally ready (CI, backups, alerting), security/compliance ready (K1-K3 hardened, PDPO, Singapore residency), commercially ready with the acceptance test: body #2 onboards without hand-holding.

nodes.label: Phase C Body engaged
nodes.rationale: The external validation gate; 7+2 questions (original seven plus external-evidence handling and session-granularity), behavioural phrasing per the Q5 rule; MCHK fallback at +2 weeks silence.

nodes.label: Phase M2 CPD engine live
nodes.rationale: Engine half (body_rules per Q26, deterministic evaluator, evaluator versioning Q27, issuance, roster, retro-trust) + governance half + debt closure; then the M2 freeze review and scoped unfreeze.

nodes.label: Phase M3 Signed & verifiable
nodes.rationale: AWS/KMS (ECC_P256 sign-only ap-east-1), sign-certificate, verify-record public URL, staff TOTP mandatory with amr-freshness gating, email cron, calendar links, unfreeze wave 1.

nodes.label: Phase D/M4 Pilot-complete lean cut
nodes.rationale: Thin UI slice (organiser accreditation UI + CPD Ledger wallet v1) + 2 real accredited events + evidence pack accepted + invoice paid; auditor portal/external activities/session UI/AI deferred to E.

nodes.label: Phase E Production-ready
nodes.rationale: Waves: external activities + evidence locker, session/track model, auditor portal, org self-serve admin, comms v2, reports v2 + zh-HK, production hardening; B7 AI/B8 detection demand-triggered, possibly post-E.

nodes.label: Block map (K1-K3 kernel / B1-B8 domain blocks)
nodes.rationale: B1 events/attendance, B2 registry, B3 credit engine incl. external activities + evidence locker, B4 certification + public verify, B5 comms, B6 auditor evidence; B7 AI/B8 detection advisory-by-design and demand-triggered.
nodes.norm_label: block map (k1-k3 kernel / b1-b8 domain blocks)

nodes.label: Cross-phase invariants
nodes.rationale: Three-lens phase-completion + live backtest; three-layer validation; audited definer functions audit-insert-last; Hard Rule 11 with negative tests; frontend freeze until M2; Q26 before anything config-referencing; no deploy by momentum.

nodes.label: Q30 Payments (Stripe pass-through, HKMA-avoidance)
nodes.rationale: Stripe as placeholder only, no build now; hard constraint structured to avoid HKMA regulation - pass-through processing, Eventar never holds client money, no stored-value mechanics; invoice-first through E.

nodes.label: CPD Frontend Design Exploration
nodes.rationale: Exploratory design study in parallel with the backend build; no repo frontend touched, the freeze holds; deliverable is a published mockup artifact feeding the M2 unfreeze scope.

nodes.label: Practitioner CPD Ledger surface (lead)
nodes.rationale: Compliance-cycle-first: cycle progress ring + category-threshold bars + verified-vs-self-reported banner, then the append-only ledger; beats the competitor's no-deadline weakness. Cycle-with-deadline is the unit of meaning, not cumulative total.

nodes.label: Organiser Accreditation & Compliance surface
nodes.rationale: Event-accreditation-centric, enriched with the forms' category/threshold vocabulary; roster eligibility as a stacked meter - eligibility is a property of the row, not a report you run.

nodes.label: Event Schedule single + multi-track
nodes.rationale: Multi-track needs sessions with start/end times, parallel tracks/rooms, and role-typed people - a richer schema than the current single-track agenda-block model; a data-model decision to make deliberately before building toward it (CLAUDE.md rule 13).

nodes.label: Practitioner wallet / QR pass
nodes.rationale: The mobile attendee surface; the personal QR turns registered into a first-party attendance fact when scanned; points show pending on the pass then posted in the ledger the moment check-in happens. QR rendered white-always (scannable regardless of theme).

nodes.label: Landing page
nodes.rationale: White-ground marketing surface; comparison strip is the competitor research verbatim (self-report to 30-day verification vs scan to real-time hash-chained); honesty guardrails - rule-aware for 8 bodies means encoded rulebooks, not endorsements; no invented client counts.

nodes.label: Palette: white ground + blue ramp
nodes.rationale: v3 (2026-07-16) locked one blue ramp with fixed roles (#1C3C94 primary, #0E79EC links/CTA, #4494BC icons/borders, #6CAAEF hover) replacing teal; status colours stay semantic; Eventar surfaces load white for everyone, dark is an explicit user choice never an OS/host inheritance.

nodes.label: App-shell architecture (global shell, pages swap)
nodes.rationale: Shell renders once with pages swapping inside it (URL updates, shell never moves); venue status indicator (Connected/Offline/Syncing) as a first-class shell element since offline tolerance is the #1 live-ops risk.

nodes.label: Provenance chip (scanned at venue / self-reported)
nodes.rationale: One of the two product-spine primitives (with the eligibility flag) missing from the minimum set; repeats across roster/ledger/wallet/check-in; first-party scanned-at-venue provenance is the one thing the incumbent structurally cannot show.

nodes.label: Landing aesthetic Option D White stage
nodes.rationale: Ivan's between B & C, white as the main color; B's white ground + glass nav + soft washes carrying C's drama on white (masked dot-matrix, bold-sans + serif-italic headline, dark-bezel laptop frame); candidate for the aesthetic lock.
nodes.norm_label: landing aesthetic option d white stage

nodes.label: Frontend freeze (holds until M2 review)
nodes.rationale: These mockups are a design target, not shippable code; the unfreeze build translates them onto the real token grid honouring the shipped component API.

nodes.label: Roadmap to MVP (consolidated spine)
nodes.rationale: One milestone spine unifying backend milestones M1-M4, POC/engagement milestones A-D, and the market-realignment backlog; MVP = a runnable paid pilot with one real accrediting body.

nodes.label: Consolidated milestone spine (M1/A-E)
nodes.rationale: M1 shipped, A demo-ready, B field-proven, C body engaged, M2 CPD engine live, M3 signed & verifiable, D/M4 pilot-complete, E CPD platform not event tool.

nodes.label: Lean first-pilot MVP cut
nodes.rationale: 3b + Sprint 4 signing + a thin organiser/attendee UI slice; auditor portal, AI tagging, detection pipeline manual/deferred for pilot #1 (hand-generate the first evidence pack); recommended cut.

nodes.label: Full M4 cut
nodes.rationale: Everything through Sprint 5 + full unfreeze; the real product, wanted before onboarding bodies #2/#3 unattended.

nodes.label: External body review is the long pole
nodes.rationale: Wall-clock is gated on two external things not code: the body review (isn't scheduled, engineering can't shorten it) and the HKCP CPD manual Ivan sources; the single highest-leverage move is scheduling the review.
nodes.norm_label: external body review is the long pole

nodes.label: Decisions that gate sprints

nodes.label: Role-Split Refactor (scoped inventory)
nodes.rationale: Scoping only, no code; re-entry when the platform-role/body-label split is prioritised; exists so the refactor is scoped not discovered mid-flight (the exact underestimate that made the Sprint 3a role-widen cost real review effort).

nodes.label: Platform-role enum vs body-specific labels
nodes.rationale: A hardwired platform-role enum (maps to RLS) separate from configurable body-specific role labels; a new body's vocabulary becomes mapping rows, not a migration.

nodes.label: Three role-resolution indirection points
nodes.rationale: is_manager(), is_eventar_staff(), require_active_staff(); the blast radius is real but partially pre-consolidated - most sites already route through these three choke points, so the refactor extends them rather than rewriting dozens of scattered comparisons.

nodes.label: Definer functions passing raw role literals
nodes.rationale: transition_dsr, mark_attended, publish_event, verify_licence, lapse_licence, revoke_licence pass literal args to require_active_staff; pseudonymise_user has an inline check; args become platform-role enum values with body labels resolved before the call.
